dm4.name: Data Center revenue growth vs the prior quarter
dm4.measured_against: the prior quarter (written exception to the year-earlier default, Kenneth 5 Oct 2026)
dm4.what: How fast Nvidia's Data Center sales grew from one quarter to the next.
dm4.why: At +117% vs a year earlier, year-on-year growth would read strong for quarters after the AI build-out peaks; quarter-on-quarter growth shows a slowdown two to three quarters sooner.
dm4.bull_means: The AI build-out is still growing fast quarter to quarter.
dm4.neutral_means: Growth is slowing to single digits per quarter.
dm4.bear_means: Data Center sales are flat or falling: the classic sign of a capex peak.

dm4.name: ACIE revenue growth (demand beyond the big clouds)
dm4.what: Growth in Data Center sales to customers other than the giant clouds (AI clouds and start-ups, sovereign AI, industrial and enterprise) vs the same quarter last year.
dm4.why: Shows whether demand is broadening beyond four or five buyers who are also building their own chips. Part of ACIE is AI clouds that Nvidia invests in or guarantees, so strong ACIE growth is not purely independent demand.
dm4.bull_means: Demand is spreading widely beyond the big clouds.
dm4.bear_means: Nvidia is back to depending on the big clouds.

dm5.name: Big-4 cloud capital spending (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta)
dm5.source: The four companies' quarterly results and SEC filings
dm5.measured_against: same calendar quarter a year earlier
dm5.latest: about +79% (Jun 2026 quarter: $170.1bn vs about $95.0bn a year earlier; Alphabet cash capex only)
dm5.what: Combined capital spending (data centres and equipment) of the four biggest cloud buyers in the latest quarter vs the same quarter a year earlier.
dm5.why: It is Nvidia's customers' budget, reported by the customers, and it arrives before Nvidia reports.
dm5.bull_means: Customer budgets are still growing fast.
dm5.bear_means: Budgets are close to flat, which historically comes before chip orders fall.

mix._note: Revenue mix (not scored). Nvidia changed its market-platform reporting in Q1 FY27: Data Center (split into Hyperscale and ACIE, only 4 quarters published) and Edge Computing. Edge Computing = the old Gaming + Professional Visualization + Automotive + OEM & Other lines (checked: Q1 FY26 4,950 and Q2 FY26 5,647 match exactly), so the second pattern rebuilds its history.
mix.note: Nvidia reports profit only for its two legal segments (Compute & Networking; Graphics), which do not line up with Data Center and Edge Computing, so both parts show the whole-company gross margin (marked *). The Hyperscale / ACIE split of Data Center is published only from FY26 comparatives (4 quarters) and is tracked in DM4b instead.
